final_selection.universe_question: What happens after a mine, dam, cable, factory, or software system is no longer useful to its original owner but remains physically or institutionally present?
final_selection.route_question: How does an orphaned oil well become a public problem decades after the company that drilled it disappears?
final_selection.distinct_engine: The environmental and financial afterlife of extraction is more about legal disappearance than physical drilling; plugging costs land on the public.
final_selection.second_act: The same legal-disappearance mechanism leaves the public holding reclamation costs at abandoned coal mines and orphaned Superfund sites, so the oil-well story opens into a broader afterlife-of-extraction pattern.
